overall: The AG resolved the complaint by informal action, finding the Board violated the OML by failing to name the bargaining unit for a Purpose 3 executive session, but found no violation on late minutes approval.

allegations.summary: Board convened executive session Sept 6 under Purpose 3 (collective bargaining) without identifying the bargaining unit in the notice or pre-session announcement.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to identify the bargaining unit to be discussed in executive session

allegations.summary: Board did not approve minutes of its July 30 retreat in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Board timely approved the minutes of the July 30 retreat when it approved those minutes at its September 6 meeting, the third meeting following the retreat.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
Within 30 days of the letter, disclose to the public at an open session meeting the identity of the bargaining unit discussed in executive session on September 6.
